newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong earthquake hits Japan's southern island.
newsitem.headline: Strong earthquake hits Japan's southern island.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook Japan's southernmost main island of Kyushu on Tuesday morning but there were no immediate reports of damage, authorities said.
Japan's Metereological Agency said the quake, which struck at 7:18 a.m. (2218 GMT), registered five on Japan's seven point scale in the city of Miyazaki. A five can violently shake houses.
Reporters for NHK television in the city of Miyazaki said there was violent shaking but there was no visible damage in the center of the city.
They said fire engines and ambulances patrolled the streets looking for fires or building collapses.
Utility companies said there was no damage to electrical systems or gas lines.
The quake measured 6.3 on the open-ended Richter scale and was centered 30 km (18 miles) off the coast.
